about: One entry per rater file. Append new entries at the end; do not edit or reorder old ones. See README.md.

rounds.items: 210 findings drawn with seed 1 from the essay and docs categories of the evaluation corpus
notes: Items are keyed by the first 16 hex digits of a hash of the text id, the rule and the sentence. The sample file is kept with the fetched corpus, outside the repository, so rule, stratum and kind are null here; every item is a finding.
Rater 1 (claude-opus) labelled first; Codex and the eight OpenRouter models labelled later, blind to the other labels.

rounds.items: 597 items: findings and decoys (random span, longest sentence) from READMEs (S1) and docs files (S2)
notes: Raters 1 to 3 are the first round; raters 4 to 12 and blind 1 to 3 were added by the amendment of 19 November 2026 written after the first three raters and before any of their labels existed.
One Haiku rater (7, 8 or 9; which one is not recorded) wrote its last batch before reading the items and then rewrote it from the sentences; its labels are kept as it left them (docs/evaluation.md).

rounds.items: 875 items: findings, near misses and random decoys across every format readcost reads
notes: The sample holds item 768685 twice, so raters saw 876 rows; every rater gave both copies the same label. labels.jsonl has one row per item and rater and keeps the first copy.

rounds.items: 1,694 items: 1,153 findings, near misses and random decoys for every rater, and 541 ranked sentences for the unprimed raters only
notes: All fifteen label files cover every item meant for them exactly once.

raters.rubric: scripts/second_rater.py (RUBRIC), which that script says is the rubric the first rater used; docs/evaluation.md (Method, step 3)
raters.run: the session's model, labels written by hand in analysis/labels.py, outside the repository
